low frequency vibration (LFFV) causes a decrease in activity of the enzymes involved in energy metabolism in neurons of the nucleus of anterior vestibularis.
the activities of dehydrogenases of the neurons in the NVA are increased under the influence of vibration, and that the sizes of subpopulation of neurons with increased activity are increased.
the activities of NADPH, NADN and succinate-DH are increased in NVA neurons after 30 min exposure to low frequency vibrations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the main changes in the activities of NADN-DH and NADPH-DDH were observed in the neurons of NVA under the influence of the low frequency vibration.

the main changes in the activities of NADN-, NADPH-, beta-oxybutirrate-, succinate-, alpha-glycerolphosphat-, glutamate- and malate-dehydrogenases in NVA neurons were observed under the influence of vibration.

low frequency vibration (20-50 Hz) causes the activation of oxidative metabolism in the majority of NVA neurons and a decrease of their activity in the neurons with a low level of oxidative metabolism, which may be a compensatory mechanism for the maintenance of the functional state of the vestibular system under the influence of the vibration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activities of all the enzymes studied are changed in the neurons of NVA.
the activity of NADN-DH in neurons of the NVA is increased by 1.5-2.0 times in response to the vibration.
the activity of NADPH-DPH, malate-DPH, succinate-DPH, beta-oxy-butyrate-DPH and glutamate-DH in NVA neurons increases under the influence of vibration.
